key_insight: grapheme-kit shifts text evaluation from Unicode code points to grapheme clusters, making multilingual metrics more faithful to how characters are actually perceived and written. This is especially important for scripts where one visible character can be made of multiple code points, such as Tamil and Sinhala.
problem_solved: Many NLP distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics miscount errors in languages whose writing systems use multi-code-point graphemes. This can lead to inaccurate scoring, poor analysis of model outputs, and misleading comparisons across multilingual text.
method: Reimplements common lexical distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics to operate on grapheme clusters instead of raw Unicode code points.
Adds improved grapheme processing utilities for Tamil and Sinhala, including grapheme cluster identification and grapheme composition/decomposition.
Provides an open-source Python library for integrating grapheme-aware text processing into multilingual NLP pipelines.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means more accurate evaluation of spelling, transliteration, normalization, and generation tasks in multilingual settings. It reduces hidden errors caused by Unicode-level mismatch and improves fairness across scripts.
